newsitem.title: FRANCE: Jospin narrowly favoured over Juppe for PM - poll.
newsitem.headline: Jospin narrowly favoured over Juppe for PM - poll.

text.p: French voters narrowly favour Socialist Lionel Jospin as prime minister over incumbent Alain Juppe but more than a third are indifferent to next month's election, opinion polls showed on Tuesday.

An IFOP poll for VSD magazine showed 39 percent of respondents wanted a victory for the governing centre-right, and 33 percent a leftist win. The snap parliamentary elections will be held in two rounds on May 25 and June 1.
The same suvey showed that Jospin was the best prime minister for France according to 37 percent of voters. Thirty-four percent picked Juppe and 21 percent favoured neither.
A Sofres poll for the daily Le Monde found more than a third of voters believed neither the centre-right nor the left would address their concerns.
The poll found that voters had slightly greater confidence in the ruling coalition to run France than in the Socialists, but neither party had the confidence of most French people.
Thirty-five percent supported the centre-right, 32 percent the Socialists and 31 percent had confidence in neither.

Another SOFRES poll for the business weekly L'Usine Nouvelle showed that tax cuts should be the new government's priority for 52 percent of voters, with wage increases to boost consumer demand the next priority for 44 percent.
